source: can u make a word game to see if you can spell the word that shows up on the screen 3rd person and realistic and it's a beach with a sea outlook and you sit on beach chairs and a voice says a word and you type it in and it tells you if it's right or wrong and you collect points

image_prompt.text: A stretch of beach where players gather, the chairs clustered so everyone faces the water
The sand split into even, easily identifiable quadrants for answer tiles
a realistic beach of soft sand looking out over an open sea to the horizon
beach chairs set along the shore facing the water

layout_placement.text: seat markers on the beach chairs so players can sit down to play

notes: Considered P5 - a spelling game is normally a UI surface with no space - but the user asked for a third-person beach they sit in, which is a place, so it builds. Same call as the origami-in-a-studio example.

Classification was genuinely ambiguous: Puzzle carries a Word / Quiz preset, while both Puzzle and Party & Casual say a quiz with no physical puzzle elements belongs in Party & Casual. Followed the boundary note.
The layout job here is very small - a beach, some chairs, and somewhere to look while the word is read out.

open_questions.ask: Is this one small stretch of beach with a few chairs, or a longer shoreline players can walk along between words?
Is everyone spelling the same word at once and racing, or does each player get their own?

theme: Realistic seaside - soft sand, open water, natural daylight

answers.ask: Is this one small stretch of beach with a few chairs, or a longer shoreline players can walk along between words?
answers.answer: Make it one small stretch of beach with a few beach chairs and a sea outlook, so players stay focused on the spelling game.

answers.ask: Is everyone spelling the same word at once and racing, or does each player get their own?
answers.answer: Everyone should hear and spell the same word at once, with points awarded for correct answers.
